description: Windstorm Pit Stop, a context optimizer for Claude Code. Use when the user says "pit stop", "/pit-stop checkup", "/pit-stop setup", "/pit-stop status", "/pit-stop report", "/pit-stop optimize", "/pit-stop reading" or "/pit-stop restart", or asks to tune when a session auto-compacts, set an idle point or a compaction window (300K/500K/700K), stop sessions compacting mid-task, check why sessions are not on the newest Claude Code, keep many sessions updated without watching them, check or trim MEMORY.md / CLAUDE.md so they load fully, or suggest a model and effort for a session's job. Also use right after installing this plugin for the user, to run the checkup first and show it.

per_query.query: run a pit stop on this machine and tell me what you find
can you do the /pit-stop checkup for me? I want to see how my sessions are doing
My Claude Code sessions keep auto-compacting right in the middle of a long refactor and then lose track of what they were doing. Can you make them wait until I'm between tasks?
set the compaction window for this folder to 500K, the default compacts way too early for the kind of work I do here
Why are my long-running claude sessions still on 2.1.300 when 2.1.330 is out? I've got about 12 of them open in tmux and none of them moved.
I run around 20 Claude Code agents on one server and I can't babysit them. I want them all to end up on the newest Claude Code without me watching or interrupting their work.
my MEMORY.md has gotten really long. is it even loading fully at session start anymore? trim it if it isn't
this session is going to spend the next week triaging logs and opening tickets. which model and effort level should it run at so I'm not overpaying?
I just installed the Windstorm Pit Stop plugin. What now?
When a session in this repo goes quiet it compacts itself at about 200K. I'd rather it waited longer here. Can you change the idle point?
